property_summary: When calling transfer with at least one element in _tos and _tos length > 0, the reference returns true but the mutant returns false.

When calling transfer from an address other than the hardcoded from address (0x9797...), the reference contract reverts due to the require statement, while the buggy contract does not revert and executes the calls.

When _tos.length == 0, the original contract reverts at require(_tos.length > 0) while the buggy contract does not revert (since the loop condition i <= _tos.length allows i=0 and attempts _tos[0] out-of-bounds, but the call reverts on its own, and the transfer function does not revert because the revert is not caught; however the key observable difference is that the original contract reverts entirely when _tos is empty, while the buggy contract does not revert and returns true, making the return value differ).

When _tos has exactly 1 element, the reference contract's loop runs only once (i=0) while the buggy contract runs twice (i=0 and i=1), causing an out-of-bounds array access on _tos[1] that reverts the call; the reference returns true, the buggy call reverts, thus the return value diverges.
